title: Se me olvidó: accidental se, datives and leísmo
summary: Say things happened to you (se me olvidó), stress the whole action (comerse), show who is affected (no me llores), and know when le, lo and la are standard.
focus: Accidental se, aspectual se, datives of interest, leísmo and laísmo
content:
## Accidental se: it happened to me

In **se + indirect pronoun + verb**, the pronoun is the person it happened to, and the verb agrees with the **thing**:

| | singular thing | plural things |
|---|---|---|
| me | se me olvid**ó** la cartera | se me olvid**aron** las llaves |
| te | se te rompi**ó** el móvil | se te rompi**eron** las gafas |
| le | se le cay**ó** el vaso | se le cay**eron** los platos |
| nos | se nos acab**ó** la leche | se nos acab**aron** los huevos |

It sounds less guilty than *rompí el vaso* (I broke it). **Se** always comes first: *se me*, never *me se*.

## Aspectual se: the whole thing

Some verbs take **se** to stress that the action is complete or done with gusto. The object is then definite or counted:

- **comerse** toda la tarta, **beberse** dos litros, **leerse** un libro entero
- **saberse** la lección = know it by heart
- **irse** = to leave (*ir* = to go somewhere), **dormirse** = to fall asleep

With a bare noun there is no se: *comí pan*, but *me comí el pan*.

## Datives of interest

An extra pronoun can show who is affected, even if they are not part of the action:

- ***No me llores**.* (Don't cry; it upsets me.)
- *Mi hijo **no me come** nada.* (My son won't eat a thing, and I worry.)
- ***Se le murió** el perro.* (Her dog died, and it hit her.)
- ***Cuídamelo**.* (Look after him for me.)

## Le, lo, la: what is standard?

Standard Spanish uses **lo / la** for direct objects and **le / les** for indirect ones. There are two departures:

- **Leísmo** with a male person: *A Juan **le** vi ayer.* Common in central and northern Spain and accepted in the singular.
- **Laísmo** and **loísmo**: *la dije la verdad*, *lo dije que no*. Heard in central Spain, but non-standard. Write ***le** dije*.

A redundant **le** with a noun is normal: ***Le** di el libro **a Ana***. With a plural, careful style uses **les**: ***les** dije a mis padres*.

vocabulary.example: Se me olvidó por completo que hoy era su cumpleaños.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It completely slipped my mind that it was her birthday today.

vocabulary.example: Al camarero se le cayó la bandeja delante de todos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The waiter dropped the tray in front of everyone.

vocabulary.example: A mitad de la cena se nos acabó el vino.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Halfway through dinner we ran out of wine.

vocabulary.example: ¿Se te rompió la pantalla otra vez?

vocabulary.meaning: it occurred to me, I had an idea
vocabulary.example: Se me ocurrió una idea en la ducha.
vocabulary.example_meaning: An idea came to me in the shower.

vocabulary.meaning: they lost (it got lost on them)
vocabulary.example: A los vecinos se les perdió el gato y lo encontramos en nuestro balcón.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The neighbours lost their cat and we found it on our balcony.

vocabulary.meaning: to eat up, to eat (all of)
vocabulary.example: Los niños se comieron todas las galletas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The children ate up all the biscuits.

vocabulary.example: Se bebió el café de un trago y salió corriendo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He downed his coffee in one gulp and dashed out.

vocabulary.example: Mi sobrina se sabe todas las capitales de Europa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My niece knows all the capitals of Europe by heart.

vocabulary.example: Se fue de la fiesta sin decir adiós.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She left the party without saying goodbye.

vocabulary.example: Me dormí y llegué tarde a la entrevista.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I overslept and was late for the interview.

vocabulary.meaning: using le as a direct object for a male person (accepted in Spain)
vocabulary.example: El leísmo es muy frecuente en Madrid y en Castilla.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leísmo is very common in Madrid and Castile.

vocabulary.meaning: using la as an indirect object (non-standard)
vocabulary.example: Decir la dije en vez de le dije es un caso de laísmo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Saying la dije instead of le dije is a case of laísmo.

quiz.explanation: The verb agrees with the thing forgotten (tu cumpleaños, singular), and se always comes first.

quiz.prompt: A Pedro se ___ cayeron las gafas al río.
quiz.explanation: The person it happened to (Pedro) is the indirect pronoun le: se le cayeron.

quiz.prompt: Se nos ___ la leche; hay que comprar más.
quiz.explanation: The verb agrees with la leche (singular), not with nosotros.
hints: What ran out? One thing or several?

quiz.prompt: Which sentence presents breaking the vase as an accident?
quiz.explanation: Accidental se makes the vase the subject and the speaker the person it happened to.

quiz.prompt: Mi hijo se ___ (comer) toda la tarta él solito. (preterite)
quiz.explanation: Comerse + a whole, definite object: se comió toda la tarta.

quiz.prompt: Ana ___ a las diez sin despedirse.
quiz.explanation: To leave = irse. Ir needs a destination (fue a casa).
hints: She left; she didn't go anywhere in particular.

quiz.explanation: Decir takes an indirect object: le dije. La vi is fine because ver takes a direct object.
hints: Who is told something: direct or indirect object?

quiz.prompt: A tu hermano ___ vi ayer en el metro.
quiz.explanation: The direct object pronoun is lo; le for a male person (leísmo) is also accepted in Spain.

quiz.prompt: In 'No me llores, cariño', what does me add?
options: The speaker is emotionally affected by the crying.
The crying is aimed at the speaker as an object.
quiz.correct_answer: The speaker is emotionally affected by the crying.
quiz.explanation: This is a dative of interest: it shows who is affected, not who is the object.

listening.text: Se me ha olvidado la contraseña.
listening.note: New word: la contraseña = the password.

listening.text: Se le cayó el móvil al agua.
listening.meaning: He dropped his phone in the water.

listening.text: Me sé la canción de memoria.
listening.meaning: I know the song by heart.

listening.text: Se nos fue la luz durante la tormenta.
listening.meaning: Our power went off during the storm.

listening.text: El niño se durmió en el coche.
listening.meaning: The little boy fell asleep in the car.

listening.text: Se me ha manchado la camisa de tomate.
listening.meaning: I've got tomato on my shirt.
listening.note: New word: mancharse = to get stained.

listening.text: A mi vecina se le murió el gato la semana pasada.
listening.meaning: My neighbour's cat died last week.
listening.note: Dative of interest: she is affected.

listening.text: Cuídamelo mucho, que es lo que más quiero en el mundo.
listening.meaning: Look after him well for me, he's what I love most in the world.

guide.tip: In se me olvidó, find the thing that was forgotten. That is the subject, and the verb agrees with it.

conversations.title: One of those mornings
conversations.scenario: Marina arrives late at the office; her colleague Hugo asks what happened.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: At last! What happened to you?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Se le acabó la batería. Luego se me cayó el café encima.
lines.meaning: Its battery ran out. Then I spilt my coffee on myself.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vaya mañana. ¿Y por eso llegas a las diez?
lines.meaning: What a morning. And that's why you're arriving at ten?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No, en el metro se me olvidaron las llaves de la oficina.
lines.meaning: No, I left the office keys on the underground.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Tranquila, se me ocurrió dejar la puerta abierta.
lines.meaning: Relax, I had the idea of leaving the door open.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Gracias. ¿Y el jefe? ¿Ya se ha ido?
lines.meaning: Thanks. And the boss? Has he left already?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No, está en su despacho. Se ha comido todos los cruasanes.
lines.meaning: No, he's in his office. He's eaten all the croissants.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No me digas eso, que no he desayunado.
lines.meaning: Don't tell me that, I haven't had breakfast.

bites.title: It happened to me
bites.rule: Se + me/te/le/nos/os/les + verb: se me olvidó, se le cayó, se nos acabó. It sounds like an accident, not a deed.

bites.title: The verb agrees with the thing
bites.rule: Se me olvidó la cartera; se me olvidaron las llaves. The person is the pronoun; the thing is the subject.

bites.title: Comerse, irse, saberse
bites.rule: Se stresses the whole action: comerse toda la tarta, saberse la lección. Irse = leave; dormirse = fall asleep.

bites.title: Le, lo, la
bites.rule: Lo/la = direct object, le = indirect. Le for a man as direct object is accepted in Spain; la dije (laísmo) is not standard.
bites.example: Le dije la verdad a María.

sorts.title: Olvidó or olvidaron?
sorts.why: The verb agrees with what was forgotten; an infinitive counts as singular.

sorts.title: Standard or not?

items.text: Le dije la verdad a María.
La dije la verdad a María.
A Luis lo dije que no.

sorts.why: Le for a male direct object is accepted; la or lo for an indirect object is not.

spots.sentence: Se me olvidaron el paraguas nuevo.
spots.why: El paraguas nuevo is singular, so the verb is singular.
El vaso is singular, so the verb is singular.

spots.sentence: La dije a Marta que viniera.
spots.why: Decir takes an indirect object: le dije (la dije is laísmo).

builds.text: Me sé la lección de memoria.
builds.meaning: I know the lesson by heart.
